items: **Sequence of dynasties:** the source places the Kushanas as Maurya → Shunga → Kanva → Kushan.
**Chronology of invaders:** Greeks (326 BCE) → Sakas (1st BCE) → Kushanas (1st CE).
**Ruling house:** Kushana dynasty; the empire extended beyond India.
**Important ruler:** **Kanishka I**, the major Kushana ruler.
**Chinese connection:** Chinese texts identify Kanishka as **Yue-tche**.
Adopted the title; means "Lord of the Whole World"
First Kushana ruler to issue gold coins; introduced gold coins for regular use in India; first to issue them on a large scale
Early Kushana copper coinage; he circulated copper coins
Buddha is depicted on his coins (Kanishka → Buddha)
**Coinage:** the Indo-Greeks introduced the circulation of gold coins in NW India; the Kushanas promoted gold + copper coins on a wider scale.
**Yaudheya coins:** copper coins that depict six-headed Kartikeya with a peacock.
**Yaudheya evidence:** found in the Puranas + Ashtadhyayi, etc.; these coins are associated with the Kushana period.

parts.t: Kanishka: coronation, Saka Samvat and the conflict with China
items: **Kanishka's coronation:** 78 AD; his period is also given as the 2nd c. CE.
**Saka Samvat:** begins in 78 AD; associated with Kanishka (many historians consider him its originator); it is the National Calendar of India.

**Kushana–China conflict:** Kanishka requested marriage with a Han Princess; after refusal, the Kushanas marched against Pan Chao in 90 AD with 70,000 troops, but were defeated by a smaller Chinese force.
**Contribution:** patron of Buddhism; associated with Mahayana and Nagarjuna.
**Buddhism under Kanishka:** the Fourth Council was held during Kanishka's reign; division into Hinayana and Mahayana.
**Kashmir:** associated with the Fourth Buddhist Council under Kanishka (Kanishka → Kashmir).
**Scholars listed:** Parshva (Parsva), Ashvaghosha, Vasumitra, Nagarjuna, Charaka, Mathara and others.
Associated with the court of Kanishka; poet laureate of Kanishka. Works: Buddhacharita, Saundarananda (Buddhist Sanskrit poetry), Sariputrapakaran
Buddhist scholar associated with Kanishka's court; headed the Fourth Buddhist Council
**Patanjali** was NOT associated with Kanishka's court; he belonged to the Shunga period and authored Mahabhashya.
**Trade evidence:** the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea + the Arikamedu excavation provide evidence of ports / trading centres.
**Trade route:** Kushana trade operated through the Persian Bay and the Red Sea.
**Gandhara school:** developed / flourished during the Kushana period.
**Gandhara style:** based on the Indo-Greek style; influenced by Greek art.
**Kushana patronage:** Kanishka encouraged and protected Gandhara art.
**Two sculptural schools:** Gandhara + Mathura developed distinct styles during the Kushana period.
**Surkhi:** introduced under the Kushans; architecture; Mathura.
**Manusmriti on foreigners:** Shakas, Kushans, Hunas, Pratiharas who did not follow priestly customs / local traditions were described as "Fallen Kshatriyas".
The **Satavahanas** were the first historical ruling dynasty of the Deccan.
**Earlier link:** Simuka's predecessor was Susharma / the Kanva dynasty.
**Caste:** Brahmins are given as the caste of the Satavahanas.
**Fourfold caste system:** existed during Satavahana rule.
**Last ruler:** Pulomavi III as per the Puranas; also numbered Pulumavi IV, the last Satavahana king, of the Myakadoni inscription.
The Nanaghat inscription is important for his governance
Queen who acted as regent during the minority of her son
Defeated Nahapana; titles: **Thrisamudrapati**, **Rajaraja** (royal title), **Ekabrahmana** (interpreted as Unrivalled Brahmana)
The Nasik inscription of Gautami Balasri was issued during his reign
**Kharavela:** contemporary of the Satavahana king Satakarni (Satakarni I).
Important for Satakarni-I's governance; Satavahana administration
Mentions the military achievements of Gautamiputra Satakarni; gives him the title Ekabrahmana
V.S. Sukthankar located the Satavahanas in Bellary; "Gulmika" = Feudatory chief
Mentions the 'Nigama-sabha' of the Satavahanas; ruler Kubhiraka (3rd cent. BC)
**Nasik inscription and the guild:** Ushavadatta (Rishabhadatta) invested 2,000 Karshapanas in a weaver's guild at Govardhana; rate of interest 12% (Western Kshatrapa / Satavahana era).
The earliest epigraphic record of religious land grants is in the **Satavahana inscriptions**.
Administrative divisions of the Satavahana Empire
Military officers who administered distant Aharas (away from the capital)
Royal employees who helped in administration; consulted for important decisions
Royal employees; advisors to the administration
Royal employees; Special Officers helping the king
Looked after the administration of cities / towns
King's share in the produce raised by a peasant
Trade associations that helped the development of trade during the Satavahana period
**Rate of interest on deposits in guilds**
**Flourishing maritime trade** was a feature of the Satavahana period.
**Coins of Pulomavi & Yagnasri:** indicate Satavahana maritime trade.
Most important port; a seaport of the Satavahanas on the east coast
Roman trade centre on the eastern side
**Satavahana coinage:** Lead + Copper + Bronze + Silver + Potin.
**Major metals:** lead and copper were the major Satavahana coin metals.
**Potin:** an alloy / mixture of Copper + Tin + Lead used in Satavahana coinage.
The Satavahanas issued **no gold** coins; **nickel** was also NOT used.
**Prakrit:** the official language; all Satavahana inscriptions are in Prakrit + Brahmi script; the Satavahana rulers patronised Prakrit.
**Desi Bhaasha:** the language of the common people; belongs to the Dravidian family.
**Gatha Saptasati (Gathasaptasati):** written by Hala (Satavahana); it contained writing by women.
**Chaityams:** built by the Queens of the Satavahanas for Buddhist monks.
**Patronage:** the Satavahanas supported public arts + Buddhist architecture / sculpture.
**Amaravati Stupa:** built during Satavahana rule by the Satavahanas; Ayaka pillars representing the five key events in Buddha's life.
**Amaravati:** Buddhist stupa / Satavahana tradition (Buddhist Andhra → Amaravati).
**Aradalam:** the foundation cream of Satavahana dancers.
Oldest extant Tamil grammar; grammar + poetics
**Sangam society:** agriculture + fishing + hunting + crafts + trade.
**Karikala Chola** (Sangam period): Kallanai / Grand Anicut; irrigation and agricultural development.
Maritime trade; major western-coast Sangam port
Maritime trade; major western-coast Sangam port
Chera port; maritime trade; associated with Rome + Southeast Asia
Important Pandya port; developed Roman trade (Pandya → Port → Rome)
Maritime trade; major Chola port + capital of the early Chola kings
Cotton trade; major cotton centre; mentioned in the Periplus
**Kaveri Poompattinam / Kaveripattinam:** other names of Puhar.
**Arikamedu:** Roman trade centre on the eastern side; Roman objects found (Romans → Arikamedu).
**Chera:** trade relations with the Roman Empire in the Sangam period.

parts.t: Founder and the end of the Mauryas
items: **How:** he was the commander of the last Mauryan ruler **Brihadratha** and established the Shunga dynasty after overthrowing and killing him.
**Date:** Brihadratha was assassinated by Pushyamitra Shunga in 185 BCE; this marks the transition Maurya → Shunga.
**Capital / region:** Magadha; Agnimitra is specifically identified as the Shunga ruler of Vidisha.
**Origin:** the ancestors of the Shungas originated from Ujjain.
**Caste:** Pushyamitra Shunga is described as a Brahmin; the succeeding Kanvas are also described as Brahmins.

parts.t: Ashvamedhas, the Ayodhya inscription and Patanjali
items: **Pushyamitra Shunga** performed two Ashvamedha (Ashwamedha) Yajnas; the **Ayodhya Inscription** gives information about them.
**Patanjali:** author of Mahabhashya (grammar); belonged to the Shunga period and was a contemporary of Pushyamitra Shunga.
**Patanjali's role:** the two Ashwamedha ceremonies of Pushyamitra were organised under Patanjali's supervision.
**Agnimitra:** son of Pushyamitra (the founder); Shunga ruler of Vidisha.
**Malavikagnimitram:** by Kalidasa; its protagonist is the Shunga ruler Agnimitra; the play concerns the love story of Agnimitra of Vidisha and Malavika.
**First play:** Malavikagnimitram is the first play of Kalidasa.
**Besnagar / Vidisha:** Heliodorus Pillar / Garuda Pillar; Bhagavata religion (Heliodorus → Vidisha).
**Bharhut Stupa:** Satna, Madhya Pradesh; Shunga architecture; discovered by Alexander Cunningham.

parts.t: The last Shunga and the Kanvas
items: **Last ruler:** Devabhuti was the last ruler of the Shunga dynasty.
**End:** Devabhuti was killed by his minister / Amatya **Vasudeva Kanva**.
**Successor dynasty:** Shunga → Kanva; founder of the Kanvas: Vasudeva Kanva.

corrections.corrected: Kushana–China conflict: ... the Kushanas marched against Pan Chao in 90 AD with 70,000 troops, but were defeated by a smaller Chinese force.
corrections.checked: The Kushan march of 70,000 troops against Ban Chao is dated 90 CE (Ban Chao, Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ban_Chao ; Britannica https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ban-Chao)

corrections.title: The Kushans
corrections.rocket: KANISHKA CORONATION | 78 AD  /  Kanishka | 2nd c. CE
corrections.corrected: Kanishka's coronation: 78 AD; his period is also given as the 2nd c. CE.
corrections.checked: Both datings are in use (78 AD is the Saka-era dating; other chronologies place Kanishka in the 2nd century CE), so both are kept; not web-settled further.

corrections.corrected: Motupalli: most important port; a seaport of the Satavahanas on the east coast.
corrections.checked: Motupalli is on the seacoast in Chinnaganjam mandal, Bapatla district, on the Bay of Bengal (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motupalli)

corrections.corrected: V.S. Sukthankar located the Satavahanas in Bellary.

corrections.checked: The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela names Satakarni (identified with Satakarni I) as his contemporary, not Hala (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hathigumpha_inscription)

corrections.checked: The same last king of the main line is numbered Pulumavi III or IV in different lists; the Myakadoni inscription is his (https://ancientindia.co.in/?p=6169 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satavahana_dynasty)
